svg.text: 03 Head electronics: slip ring, PSIs, holoprojectors, logic matrices, radar eye
Twelve slip-ring wires carry everything into the dome. No multiplexer: the four backpacks use four addresses on Pi I2C-1.
SR1 Adafruit 1195 slip ring, 12 wires, 2 A each
5 V dome feed, leg 1 of 2 <- F6 fuse output (5 V rail)
5 V dome feed, leg 2 of 2 <- F6 fuse output (5 V rail)
dome return, leg 1 of 2 <- star ground TB2
dome return, leg 2 of 2 <- star ground TB2
NeoPixel data to LED1 <- KB2040 A2
I2C-1 data, four backpacks <- Pi GPIO2 (header pin 3)
I2C-1 clock, four backpacks <- Pi GPIO3 (header pin 5)
SPI0 MOSI to the TFT <- Pi GPIO10 (header pin 19)
SPI0 clock to the TFT <- Pi GPIO11 (header pin 23)
SPI0 CE0 chip select <- Pi GPIO8 (header pin 24)
Body 12.4 mm dia x 19.5 mm, no flange.
Clamped in the printed post on the
body top plate; rotor stub 4 mm.
turns the dome far slower than that.
cable tie within 40 mm of the body.
Total worst case 1.62 A on F6 2 A.
Two wires carry 5 V and two carry
the return: 4 A of slip-ring capacity.
A. NeoPixel chain, one data wire, five devices
DIN to DOUT in that order. 5 V and ground for every device come from the dome 5 V bus (slip-ring wires 1-4), never from the data wire's neighbour.
B. Logic matrices on Pi I2C-1 and the radar-eye TFT on Pi SPI0
front logic, upper window - address jumpers: none bridged
front logic, lower window - address jumpers: A0 bridged
rear logic, left half - address jumpers: A1 bridged
rear logic, right half - address jumpers: A0 and A1 bridged
All four share slip-ring wires 6 (SDA) and 7 (SCL), daisy-chained backpack to
backpack inside the dome, plus 5 V (wire 2) and ground (wire 4).
The HT16K33 has its own 3.3 V-tolerant I2C and runs from 5 V: no level shifter.
Bridge the address pads with solder BEFORE the backpacks go behind the windows.
firmware/pi/displays.py drives 0x70/0x71 as two independent front windows and
0x72/0x73 as one 16 x 8 rear strip that scrolls across the seam.
DS5 Adafruit 6178 round TFT (GC9A01A) behind the radar lens
slip-ring wire 8 <- Pi GPIO10, header pin 19
slip-ring wire 9 <- Pi GPIO11, header pin 23
slip-ring wire 10 <- Pi GPIO8 (CE0), header pin 24
slip-ring wire 11 <- Pi GPIO25, header pin 22
slip-ring wire 12 <- Pi GPIO24, header pin 18
R1 100 ohm to the dome 5 V bus: always on
There is no thirteenth slip-ring wire, so the backlight is not switched from
the Pi. LITE goes to 5 V through R1 (100 ohm), which sets a steady, slightly
reduced brightness and survives the dome turning. firmware/pi/displays.py still
drives GPIO18 as its backlight pin; with the resistor fitted that pin controls
nothing and can be left unconnected. If a dimmable backlight is wanted later,
give up the dome index sensor wire or move to a 2-wire dome controller.
